name: horizontal-scroll
title: Horizontal Scroll
description: Full-screen colour panels, one per word, slide sideways as you scroll. Each panel carries an enormous black word across its middle and a small square photo of people working at the bottom edge.
use: A manifesto or campaign page wants bold one-word statements that travel sideways with the scroll.
avoid: The section runs five screens tall with no skip control, and every word, colour and photo is hard-coded.
a11y: Photos carry alt text, but the sideways motion ignores reduced-motion and there is no way to skip the five-screen section. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Full-height panels in coral red, blue, orange, yellow and green, each filled by a huge black word such as PASSION or WORK and a small square team photo resting at the bottom edge. A dark grid hero sits above the panels.
behaves: Scrolling down pushes the row of panels leftwards, so each full-screen colour enters from the right as the previous one leaves. Inside a panel the big word drifts a little slower than the panel itself, and the row ends after the last colour.
customise: No props: the five words, their background colours and photo links sit in the panels array, and the section height and word size are classes in the source.
weight: light: Five small photos and a scroll handler that only rewrites transforms.
